title: Bathrobe and Wine
text: “Heh…”

Here I suddenly found myself thinking… God Slayer, if you think about it, is basically Fenrir in terms of legend, I say. So, hypothetically speaking! If Father used my spear as a substitute, would it also become that kind of weapon? …? Come to think of it, when Ark used my spear, it had a similar shape, didn’t it? No, wait, that one looked more like a cursed weapon. Though it was different from an ordinary cursed weapon in various ways… Let’s suppose the spirit had shaped itself into a God Slayer form specifically suited to Ark.
“It apparently has an effect that deals massive damage to holders of Sacred Weapons.”
“Ah, I see. So it exists as a weapon for heroes, then… Maybe the original purpose was for a Seven Star Weapon hero to fight against a hero who’d fallen to darkness?”
“Maybe if the Bow Hero fully falls, it satisfies the transformation condition?”
“The part where it’s limited to Itsuki specifically bugs me, but yeah, you’re probably not wrong.”
“Actually, why didn’t it come out when fighting that person, I wonder? Wolf.”
Rabbit Guy was talking about someone, I say. Persistent as ever, going on about “that person” meaning Itsuki again.
“Woof, even if it had, I don’t think we’d have won.”
“True. No question our skill hasn’t caught up yet. The guy’s lived through countless ages and he’s still basically a child.”
Crocodile Guy, who on earth was he talking about, I wonder? Rival, perhaps?
“Rival’s only good for a Seven Star Weapon at best, I say. No way it would come out, I say.”
Even now it infuriates me that Rival houses that blasted Claw Seven Star Weapon. Do you people even understand? The Claw Seven Star Weapon resides in Wolf’s hand!
“Yeah, guess not.”
Rabbit Guy sounded oddly dismissive about it. While we were chatting away like that, we arrived at the guest room, I say. Everyone set down the luggage they’d each carried in.
“Woof, Naofumi-sama, this way.”
“Eh? Not here?”
“That’s everyone else’s room—Naofumi-sama’s is further up.”
“I’d honestly be fine with the same room as everyone else…”
Just then, Crocodile Guy and Rabbit Guy stepped in between Father and Wolf as if to keep them apart, and a glaring standoff began, I say.

“Ahem. Naofumi-sama is the great Shield Hero. This is my house here in Siltvelt, so for the sake of family tradition, clan etiquette, and faith itself, we simply cannot let it be said we failed to put him up in the finest room.”
“Heh. Depends how you spin it.”
“There’s some truth to that. But we also need to inspect the room ourselves before we can properly guard it, don’t we.”
“Ugh, so noisy.”
Amid all this bristling glaring, Panda flopped carelessly onto the bed without a care in the world and lay down, I say.
“Wow, Lars-chan just sprawling out with zero motivation is kind of soothing, isn’t it? Though, Lars-chan, shouldn’t we maybe separate the men and women, just in case?”
“What’s this bunch gonna do to me.”
“Woof? Understood. Will prepare private room. Naofumi-sama, even if something happens with Larsa, please come and sleep properly in the room I guide you to.”
“Sure, sure. Well, if she wants to do something, I’ll have to entertain her or she’ll nag me endlessly about it, so I’ll think it over.”
Panda just lay there limply, I say. No motivation whatsoever, just like Lazy Pig.
“Hold on, that joke from before… are you still going with it?”

Father was trying to rein Wolf in, but apparently Crocodile Guy, Rabbit Guy, and Wolf were glaring at each other over something else entirely, I say. It seemed like nobody understood a thing, but I figured maybe it was just my imagination. Oblivious fools! Something in my memory—maybe Rival, maybe the spear spirit—seemed to be shouting that, but surely that was just my imagination!
“If you’re gonna make a scene here it’s annoying, so hurry up and go to the room already!”
Shoo, shoo! Panda waved a hand, gesturing for Father to move along.
“Well then… anyway, Wolf and the others, if there’s a room you want to show us, let’s hurry there.”
“Woof-!”
Wolf skipped off toward the destination room, I say. How old are you, exactly? A burly wolfman skipping along looked like nothing short of a joke, I say.
“What an innocent little display.”
“You’re the only one who thinks that.”

Crocodile Guy muttered that under his breath, but Father didn’t seem to hear it, I say. And so we arrived at what was apparently the finest room in this castle-like mansion. A large room with an enormous canopy bed, I say. Through the window was a spectacular view of the surrounding landscape—not quite as high up as Siltvelt’s castle, but high enough to overlook the whole territory. A full set of furniture was present. There seemed to be additional rooms as well. One had a bath and toilet; there was also a wardrobe room, though the number of clothes in it was rather modest, I say. And then… there was even a wine rack, giving the whole place the unmistakable air of a noble’s chambers.
“Ohh… nice view.”
Father stood out on what looked like a balcony, taking in the whole panorama.
“Woof! Boast, this now Wolf’s room, master’s room!”
“Figures.”
“Thought as much.”
Rabbit Guy and Crocodile Guy both sighed, I say. Then, in a flash, Wolf stripped off his clothes and changed into a bathrobe.
“Naofumi-sama, this way! Woof! Best bed! Sleep! Best materials!”
Wolf stood in front of the bed, beckoning, I say. Excitement had made Wolf’s speech even more broken than usual.
“Ohh, it’s like a king’s bed. Real rich-person vibes, the kind you’d see in a museum.”
Father touched the bed with carefree ease, I say.
“Hm… isn’t this harder than the bed back at my family home?”
“Let’s see, let’s see.”
Rabbit Guy and Crocodile Guy casually positioned themselves on either side, making sure Wolf couldn’t close the distance, I say.
“First to claim it, hyoon!”
At this point I transformed into a usaunny and leapt onto the bed, I say. I settled down beside the pillow and gave a wink.
“Ha, Motoyasu-kun, you really do look like a stuffed animal on the pillow!”
“Woof-!”

Wolf let out a growl as if in protest, I say. But then, taking a breath to compose himself, Wolf produced a bottle of wine from who-knows-where, poured a glass, and took a sip, apparently trying to calm down.
“Ahem. Naofumi-sama will sleep in this room.”
“And Wolf?”
“It’s fine.”
“Don’t just leave it at ‘it’s fine.’”
“Tell us exactly where you intend to sleep. And what’s the meaning of already changing into a bathrobe?”

Crocodile Guy and Rabbit Guy pressed the point, I say. Wolf turned away sharply. I remembered it too, I say—back when we went deep into the mountains to fetch Rival’s parent. Apparently what Wolf wanted was to have Father sleep in the bed while Wolf lay beside him in a bathrobe with a glass of wine in hand.

“That’s obviously a joke, surely. Well, knowing Wolf, isn’t this just his own room originally? Since he’s lending it to me, and now that he’s become the Claw Hero, I suppose he’s allowed to use this room.”
“Y-yeah, that’s right.”
Wolf gave an affirmation that sounded suspiciously like damage control in response to Father’s rather dim-witted interpretation, I say.
“Wolf, if you want to take a bath, we’ll clear out first, okay? It’s a bit early to sleep anyway.”
“Woof.”
Wolf turned the same moist, pleading eyes on Father that I, in usaunny form, usually gave him, I say.
“Naofumi-sama, I want nap here, with Naofumi-sama.”
“Uh… but what about the bathrobe and the wine? Is that really a ‘nap’?”
“That’s a stretch.”
“Not happening.”
“Father, Father, it’s nice and fluffy, hyoon!”
I bounced repeatedly on the bed to make my case, I say. Father’s gaze turned toward me. Heh, the winner here is me, hyoon!
“Yeah, true. Motoyasu-kun’s using it as a trampoline.”

Act your age, eternal twenty-one-year-old! shouted the original Father from within my memories, but even that Father couldn’t tear his eyes away from my current form and antics, hyoon. Surely Big Sister and Raph-chan would smile at this too, hyoon. While I carried on like that, Wolf shed the bathrobe and changed back into his usual clothes.
